newsitem.title: UK: ScotWidows swaps 250 mln stg Euro stocks to gilts.
newsitem.headline: ScotWidows swaps 250 mln stg Euro stocks to gilts.

text.p: Scottish Widows Investment Management (SWIM) said Wednesday it has sold about 250 million stg of its European equity holdings and moved the funds into gilts.
"The money has been invested in gilts - because SWIM could not find enough attraction in any other equity market," said global strategist Robin Garrow.

SWIM made the decision, which reduces its European holdings by between 15 and 20 percent, after its recent half-yearly investment policy review. The trades were completed during the course of the week ending July 18.
"We have been overweight in Europe for some time now...But, with the European markets blazing away, this is a good time to pull back a little," Garrow said.
"We remain of the view that many equity markets offer poor value at current levels. We do not like the U.S. market and that is the same to some extent with the UK," he said.
Garrow said that more and more markets look overvalued.
"So, basically, we are putting the money into gilts - it is not that we are hugely into the gilt market but it is reasonable value."
Garrow expects a US-led correction in world markets on the order of 15-20 percent in the next six to 12 months.
"I hope sooner," he said, adding that a correction would not necessarily end the bull market but rather establish a more reasonable basis.
SWIM manages over 24 billion stg. -- James Saft, London newsroom +171 542 2734
